Decompose the predicted surface into its components

Source: R/decompose.R
bruce_decompose.Rd

Splits the posterior-mean prediction on a grid into the part explained by covariates, the city-wide daily term and the spatial field, and measures how much of the spatial variance of the surface comes from each.

Usage

bruce_decompose(
  fit,
  grid = NULL,
  domain = NULL,
  dates = NULL,
  cap = TRUE,
  resample = "average"
)

Arguments

fit

A bruce_fit.

grid

A terra::SpatRaster defining the prediction grid. Cells where its first layer is NA are skipped, so a masked raster works as a domain. NULL uses the covariate rasters' own grid.

domain

Optional polygon (sf or SpatVector) to mask the grid.

dates

Subset of the fitted days; NULL predicts all.

cap

Cap covariates to the range observed at stations and background cells (avoids extrapolating linear effects).

resample

How each covariate is brought to the grid when the grids differ: "average" (block mean) or "near" (value at the cell centre). A single value or a named vector, e.g. c(svf = "near") to keep a fine-scale covariate at its native values.

Value

An object of class bruce_decomposition: total, covariates, field (SpatRasters, one layer per day), by_covariate (list of SpatRasters, one per covariate), day_effect (one value per day), variance (one row per day) and stations (locations used in the fit, for plotting).

Details

For each day the prediction at cell \(s\) is $$\hat y(s) = \beta_0 + \underbrace{x(s)^\top\beta}_{\text{covariates}} + \underbrace{d_t}_{\text{day}} + \underbrace{w(s,t)}_{\text{field}}$$ using posterior means. The intercept and the daily term are constant in space, so the spatial variance across cells is $$\mathrm{Var}(\hat y) = \mathrm{Var}(x^\top\beta) + \mathrm{Var}(w) + 2\,\mathrm{Cov}(x^\top\beta, w).$$ share_covariates and share_field are each component's variance over var_covariates + var_field; the covariance term is reported separately so that a large overlap between the two parts is visible rather than hidden in the shares.
